paragraphs.source_en: The representations of elephants are rare on the Tassili Plateau. It would not have been easy for this large animal to reach the top of the Plateau, however it could have easily moved in the much lower and more open space of the Acacus and the Algerian Tadrart where they are also depicted. The painters could have observed elephants directly from the shelters in the Acacus and the Algerian Tadrart but it is not certain if they could have done so on the Tassili Plateau.

paragraphs.source_en: Although animals are often mixed with humans on the same walls, they do not seem to be in any direct relationship. Only in rare cases are they clearly related, for example where the two are linked by a kind of a rope. There are frequent cases of physical contact where animals and humans are superimposed but it is difficult to determine if this indicates a relationship or if the superimposition is accidental. Animals were clearly important in the Round Head art because they are often of large dimensions and they are sometimes adorned with internal decoration made of dots, V-shaped patterns or lines, similar to the body decoration of the anthropomorphic figures. Some shelters exclusively present zoomorphic figures.
